html:
The Greater Wrath was the Russian occupation of Finland from 1713 to 1721, during the Great Northern War between Sweden and Russia.

After the Swedish defeat at Poltava, Russian armies overran Finland. Under the occupation many villages were burned, and thousands of Finns, many of them children, were carried off to Russia as serfs or slaves. Many people fled to Sweden or hid in the forests.

The Treaty of Nystad in 1721 returned most of Finland to Sweden, but the southeast, including Vyborg, went to Russia. It came soon after the great famine of the 1690s and left Finland deeply scarred. A second Russian occupation, the Lesser Wrath, followed in the 1740s. See Finland.
sum: The Greater Wrath was the Russian occupation of Finland from 1713 to 1721, during the Great Northern War between Sweden and Russia.
